newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian president wants to "cleanse the system".
newsitem.headline: Indian president wants to "cleanse the system".

text.p: President Kocheril Raman Narayanan on Friday appealed to citizens to mount a national movement to cleanse India of corruption and poverty which he said had marred the country's 50 years of freedom.

In a speech prepared for delivery to a special midnight session of parliament, Narayanan lauded India's achievements in maintaining unity, deepening democracy and promoting economic growth during its half century since winning independence.
"This midnight hour, thronged with memories of the past and throbbing with significance for the future, is a golden moment in the history of India and the world," the president said.
But he urged citizens to reflect on the "shortcomings and failures" that remained in the way of progress.

"Here, though we have registered significant successes, the fact of the matter is that we have not been able to abolish poverty, ignorance and disease from among our people," said Narayanan, who was elected to the mostly ceremonial post last month.

India's first low-caste president said the average life expectancy of an Indian had more than doubled since independence to 61 years in 1994, and the Green Revolution had made the country self-sufficient in food.
But he said India's rate of progress was not adequate.
"Other countries have gone far ahead of us. We have to move faster without upsetting the delicate and complicated balance of our society," he said.
The president said he was painfully aware of the deterioration of Indian society since the days of the nation's spiritual founder, Mahatma Gandhi.
"Sheer opportunism and value-less power politics have taken over the place of principles and idealism that had been the hallmark of our social and political life," he said.
He cited violence, ill treatment of women and lower castes and corruption, which he said was "corroding the vitals of our politics and society".

A long list of senior politicians and bureaucrats have been indicted in corruption cases, including former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao. The former leader of Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's party was arrested last month in a $280-million embezzlement case.
"A social movement or a widespread national movement is needed to cleanse the system," Narayanan said, calling for an assault on illiteracy, poverty, population growth and environmental degradation.
